p1-dragons-quatorze-flammes.reliabilityNoteFr: No date; several competing origin stories, all of them reported at second hand.

p1-guerres-ghiscaries.reliabilityNoteFr: Very ancient history, known through tradition; the date is an order of magnitude only.

p1-regime-possessions.reliabilityNoteFr: The books agree in their description; some further detail was supplied by the author outside the text.

p1-mines-esclaves.reliabilityNoteFr: A tradition reported by one character (the kindly man, in Braavos).

p1-cites-filles.reliabilityNoteFr: Rests on The World of Ice & Fire alone; no dates are given except for Lorath.

p1-chandelles-villevieille.reliabilityNoteFr: Asserted by an acolyte of the Citadel in a tavern conversation; there is no other source.

p1-braavos.reliabilityNoteFr: Attested in several works; no founding date is given here.

p1-guerres-rhoynares.reliabilityNoteFr: Attested in several works; the dates are estimates.

p1-peyredragon-avant-poste.reliabilityNoteFr: Approximate date (“some two centuries before the Doom”).

p1-prophetie-or-roc.reliabilityNoteFr: Speculation by an in-world author, drawing on a lost text.

p1-fleau.reliabilityNoteFr: The event and its date are established; its cause is not.

p2-signes-et-presages.reliabilityNoteFr: Hearsay reported by one character; what the book contained is unknown.

p2-siecle-de-sang.reliabilityNoteFr: Attested in several works; its internal chronology is almost entirely undated.

p2-aurion.reliabilityNoteFr: An undated episode, known from The World of Ice & Fire.

p2-gaemon-et-successeurs.reliabilityNoteFr: A bare list given by the chronicle, with neither dates nor details.

p2-dragons-de-peyredragon.reliabilityNoteFr: The fact is established; the year of Vhagar's hatching is inferred.

p2-double-mariage.reliabilityNoteFr: The double marriage is established; its date and its motives are not.

p2-table-peinte.reliabilityNoteFr: The table is attested in several works; the travels of Aegon's youth are reported with reservations.

p2-offre-argilac.reliabilityNoteFr: Orys Baratheon's kinship with Aegon is a rumour, and is presented as one.

p3-goeville.dateNoteFr: The chronicle places the campaign in 2–1 BC without dating each battle.

p3-harrenhal.dateNoteFr: The chronicle places the campaign in 2–1 BC without dating each battle.

p3-derniere-tempete.dateNoteFr: The chronicle places the campaign in 2–1 BC without dating each battle.

p3-champ-de-feu.dateNoteFr: The chronicle places the campaign in 2–1 BC without dating each battle.

p3-torrhen-stark.dateNoteFr: The chronicle places the campaign in 2–1 BC without dating each battle.

p3-eyrie.dateNoteFr: The chronicle places the campaign in 2–1 BC without dating each battle.

p3-rhaenys-dorne.dateNoteFr: The chronicle places the campaign in 2–1 BC without dating each battle.

p3-trone-de-fer.reliabilityNoteFr: The number of swords (“a thousand”) belongs to tradition.

tv-p3-reve-aegon.reliabilityNoteFr: The books give no certain motive for the Conquest; the chronicle says only that Aegon's reasons are debated.

p4-guerre-dornienne.reliabilityNoteFr: The contents of the letter are unknown; the chronicle lists several hypotheses without settling on any of them.

p4-denfert.reliabilityNoteFr: The exact fate of Rhaenys after the fall is not known.

p4-soulevement-foi.reliabilityNoteFr: The cause of Aenys's death is disputed: illness in most accounts, rumours of poison in others.

p4-mort-maegor.reliabilityNoteFr: The death is certain, its cause is not: the chronicle reports several versions.

p4-aerea-balerion.reliabilityNoteFr: The flight and the return are established; where she went and how she died rest on Barth's testimony.

p4-grand-conseil-101.reliabilityNoteFr: The outcome is established; the reported share of the votes is no more than rumour.

p5-mariage-laenor.reliabilityNoteFr: The marriage is established; the paternity of the three princes is a rumour, which the witnesses report in different ways.

p5-printemps-rouge.reliabilityNoteFr: The events are established; who was behind Laenor's death and the burning of Harrenhal remains unknown, and several suspects are named.

p5-mort-viserys.reliabilityNoteFr: The king's death and the council are established; Beesbury's death is told in three ways (throat cut, thrown from a window, a dungeon cell).

p5-accalmie.reliabilityNoteFr: The outcome is established; the details of the pursuit vary from one account to another.

p5-sang-et-fromage.reliabilityNoteFr: The murder is established; the detail of the scene comes mostly from the fool Mushroom.

p5-semailles.reliabilityNoteFr: The true descent of the “seeds” (Targaryen or Velaryon bastards) is disputed by the witnesses.

p5-gosier.dateNoteFr: Fire & Blood dates the battle to the fifth day of 130 AC; The World of Ice & Fire places it in 129.
p5-gosier.reliabilityNoteFr: The two works disagree on the date; the exact cause of Vermax's fall is uncertain.

p5-peyredragon-reprise.reliabilityNoteFr: The death of Grey Ghost was at first wrongly blamed on the Cannibal.

p5-oeildieu.reliabilityNoteFr: The outcome is established; Daemon's survival belongs to song.

p5-fossedragon.reliabilityNoteFr: Who killed Syrax? The chronicle gives at least five versions. Helaena's death (suicide or murder) is disputed as well.

p5-tumbleton-2.reliabilityNoteFr: Daeron's death comes in three versions: struck down by a sellsword, killed by a soldier who did not recognize him, or crushed beneath his burning tent.

p5-mort-aegon-ii.reliabilityNoteFr: Death by poison is established; who administered it is not.

p5-bilan-dragons.reliabilityNoteFr: The final fate of Sheepstealer, the Cannibal and Silverwing is not known.

p5-dernier-dragon.reliabilityNoteFr: The date and the description are established; the cause of death rests only on rumour and on one character's accusation.

p6-regence.reliabilityNoteFr: Jaehaera's death (officially a suicide, suspected to be murder) has never been explained.

p6-baelor.reliabilityNoteFr: Death from fasting is the received version; poisoning is a rumour.

p6-aegon-iv.reliabilityNoteFr: The claim that Daeron II was a bastard is a reported slander, never proven.

p6-troisieme-feunoyr.reliabilityNoteFr: Known only from a single brief summary, with no detailed account.

p6-quatrieme-feunoyr.reliabilityNoteFr: Known only from a single brief summary.

p6-lestival.reliabilityNoteFr: The fire and its victims are established; its cause is deliberately left obscure in the books.

p7-rhaegar-elia.reliabilityNoteFr: Rhaegar's belief is reported by Aemon and through a vision of Daenerys; what exactly he believed is not known.

p7-harrenhal-281.reliabilityNoteFr: Rhaegar's intentions (and the rumour of a secret council against his father) are matters of conjecture.

p7-lyanna.reliabilityNoteFr: That they disappeared is established; the nature of the disappearance (abduction or willing flight) is not.

p7-premieres-batailles.reliabilityNoteFr: The order of the battles is established; their exact dates are not given.

p7-sac.reliabilityNoteFr: The death of the infant Aegon is taken for granted in Westeros; a character in a later volume claims that another child was put in his place (see Period VIII).

p7-tour-de-la-joie.reliabilityNoteFr: Source: the memory and the dream of a single character. Why the Kingsguard were there is not established.

p7-naissance-daenerys.reliabilityNoteFr: Facts reported by Daenerys from what her brother used to tell her; the year is inferred.

p7-exil.reliabilityNoteFr: Daenerys's childhood memories; the years are reconstructed.

p8-noces-oeufs.reliabilityNoteFr: Where the eggs really came from is not established: there is only Illyrio's word for it.

p8-eclosion.reliabilityNoteFr: What made the hatching possible is not explained. The author has stated outside the books that Daenerys's surviving the fire was a unique event, not a lasting gift.

p8-qarth.reliabilityNoteFr: Visions seen by a single character; their meaning is open to interpretation.

p8-chandelles-brulent.reliabilityNoteFr: That a candle is burning is seen by one character as a witness; its powers rest only on Marwyn's word. The link with the return of the dragons is an inference, not something the text states.

p8-mort-aemon.reliabilityNoteFr: The death is established; the reading of the prophecy is Aemon's own.

p8-dragons-enchaines.reliabilityNoteFr: Drogon's guilt rests on the father's word; Daenerys accepts it as true.

p8-jeune-griff.reliabilityNoteFr: His claim runs counter to the accepted account of Aegon's death in 283. No proof is offered either way.
